whatIs: PocketBase is an open-source backend distributed as a single executable written in Go that uses SQLite. It includes a database with real-time subscriptions, email and OAuth2 authentication, file storage (local or S3), an admin dashboard, and a REST API, with official SDKs for JavaScript and Dart.

It's a good fit for prototypes, personal projects, and small or medium apps that need a complete backend without setting up several services. You can also use it as a Go framework or extend it with JavaScript hooks.
uses: Spinning up the backend of a Flutter mobile app with login and file storage.
Prototyping an MVP with React, Vue, or Svelte without setting up a separate server or database.
Offering real-time updates in an internal tool by subscribing to changes in a collection.
caveats: Until it reaches v1.0.0, backward compatibility isn't guaranteed, so breaking changes may appear when you upgrade.
Because it's a single process with SQLite, scaling horizontally is more limited than with a traditional backend.
You host and back it up yourself: there's no official cloud to handle that for you.
pricingNote: Open source under the MIT license, with no paid plans.
idealFor: Small projects and prototypes that need a complete backend in a single file.
